summary.headline: Mphasis Q1 FY27 revenue $471M, up 8.3% YoY constant currency; net new TCV $461M; FY27 guidance maintained at high-single to low-double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Mphasis reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $471M, up 2.1% QoQ and 8.3% YoY in constant currency, with Direct revenue at $465M. Net new TCV was $461M, the fifth straight quarter above $400M, and three large deals were closed including one above $100M. EBIT margin fell 60 bps QoQ, absorbing ramp-up costs for new deals and TAP acquisition costs, and EPS declined 4% QoQ to INR 25.6. Management maintained FY27 guidance of high-single to low-double-digit constant currency growth and a 14.75%-15.75% EBIT margin band, and guided Q2 to its best sequential constant currency growth in three years.

segments.name: Americas (Direct)
segments.commentary: Primary growth engine; grew 3.9% QoQ and 11.4% YoY in constant currency.

segments.name: ROW
segments.commentary: Grew 6.1% QoQ in constant currency, led by GCC ecosystem.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.commentary: Impacted by revenue moving to other geographies for a globally structured deal; management says underlying health intact.

segments.name: Enterprise Applications (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 11.9% YoY, driven mainly by AI-led modernization deals.

segments.name: BPO (Direct)
segments.commentary: Standout service line: 12.7% QoQ and 14% YoY growth, led by AI-led propositions.

segments.name: BFS (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 9.4% YoY and 0.8% QoQ; management cites over 3.5% compound quarterly growth across eight quarters.

segments.name: Insurance
segments.commentary: Grew 17.8% YoY but down 3.1% QoQ in constant currency after four quarters of strong growth; management attributes dip to project milestone completions.

segments.name: TMT
segments.commentary: Up 16.4% QoQ and 13.6% YoY in constant currency as recent deal wins ramped.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Grew 5.2% QoQ on new Retail deal wins; Logistics and Transportation hit by geopolitical impact.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at high-single-digit to low-double-digit in constant currency.
FY27 EBIT margin target maintained within 14.75%-15.75%, with platform investments continuing.
Q2 FY27 expected to deliver best sequential constant currency growth in three years.
Operating cash flow conversion expected at about 80% of net income through FY27.
Red Oak vendor-consolidation deal included in outlook; work expected to start around end-August, so only partial Q2 contribution.
Hedge losses expected to trend down over a couple of quarters if rupee stays near current levels; cumulative OCI hedge losses fell about INR 50 crore March to June.
Management expects margin normalization over the year as utilization recovers and Insurance transformation ramp costs normalize over the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Utilization dropped sharply in Q1 in anticipation of Q2 growth; management views this as reversible over the year.
Headcount increased in Q1 to support expected growth trajectory.
Large deals require upfront capital investment spread over 12-18 months; this drives FY27 OCF softness, with normalization expected from FY28.
FDE (forward deployed engineer) pods of 3-5 people planned for early onshore platform deployment; scale delivery remains onsite-offshore.
demand_pricing: Pipeline at all-time high, up 2.8x since Mphasis.ai launch; total pipeline up 8% QoQ and 28% YoY; non-BFS pipeline up 18% QoQ; deals above $20M up 10% QoQ; BFS pipeline up 100% YoY.
AI-led deals grew from 12% to 70% of pipeline; 63% of Q1 TCV wins were AI-led.
Mphasis Tria launched; multiple opportunities moved from conversation to closure within seven weeks; ARR and managed services bundled in Tria deals.
Management says competitive intensity in traditional renewals is rising; company says it avoids price competition and is pursuing outcome-based pricing.
Client top-tier: Top 1-10 accounts grew 11.1% YoY; Top 11-30 grew 21.0% YoY; one client dropped out of the $150M+ band on TTM ranking.
Management says clients are asking for outcome-based pricing rather than effort-based; some Q1 deals already priced that way.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Insurance and Logistics weakness was unanticipated, and is client caution rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Insurance dip reflects project milestone completions after about 35% growth in FY26, with no single-client impact; Logistics is a smaller unit affected by macro and geopolitics. It said the environment is similar to peers, with interest rates and geopolitics as key uncertainties.

qa_highlights.question: How much does the Red Oak consolidation add to FY27 growth, and is organic growth on track?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Red Oak is baked into the outlook but consummation is pending, with work expected to start around end-August. Payout is typically 1x-1.2x revenue, so the impact is within the existing guidance range and not separately quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and how does the margin path look?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said TAP acquisition earn-out cost hit margin by about 0.35%, with two-thirds of potential consideration in earn-out flowing through the P&L. A steep utilization drop, made in anticipation of growth, is expected to reverse over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF soften and when does it normalize?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about $14M of contract acquisition payments and annual variable pay in Q1 drove the softness. He reiterated about 80% OCF conversion, with normalization expected in FY28 as upfront capital in large deals is recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedge loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects hedge losses to trend down if the rupee stays near current levels, but the margin benefit will take a couple of quarters to show and will not fully disappear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of customer-contract acquisition deals?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said most upfront costs are expensed, and deals are assessed to be profitable in line with company average after that, with the first three months possibly lower or higher. Management said it does not buy low-margin businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the TTM TCV-to-revenue correlation fall from above 0.9 to 0.74?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects a higher mix of short-burst, early-deployment deals that are consumed within a quarter or two, such as 12-16 week foundation builds followed by waves of scale deployment.

risks_watch: Insurance segment margin pressure from transformation program ramp; management expects normalization over the next two quarters.
Q2 growth depends on Red Oak start (around end-August) and on ramp of recent large deals.
Pricing pressure in traditional renewals; outcome-based pricing and ARR attach must show up over the next 2-3 quarters.
Macro risks flagged by management: interest rate reversal, oil shock, geopolitics, and AI disruption fears in long-term annuity deals.
OCF weakness: DSO at 95 days; watch for progressive improvement and whether OCF conversion holds at about 80%.
Hedge losses continue to weigh on operating margin for a couple of quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on pipeline, deal momentum, and Tria traction, while cautious on the macro and explicit that margin is being deliberately invested in. Management was evasive when asked to quantify Red Oak's contribution and the FY27 revenue impact of customer-contract acquisitions, pointing to the guidance range instead.
key_quotes: Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years.
We remain committed to operating within the target band of 14.75% to 15.75% for FY27 while making the investments the platform requires.
That is not a normal sales cycle. That is demand compression.

financial_highlights.change: Fifth consecutive quarter above $400M; TTM TCV over $1.8B
Expected to improve progressively through FY27

growth.why: FY27 constant-currency growth guidance of high-single to low-double digits (midpoint ~8%) was held, backed by a record $461M net new TCV, a pipeline up 28% YoY and Q2 guided to best sequential growth in three years; no new capacity was disclosed, and utilisation dropped in Q1 as the company ramped headcount ahead of expected growth.
